title: Salsa Verde Chicken Crock
seoTitle: Salsa Verde Chicken Crock | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Tender green-chile chicken for tacos and bowls
subtitle: Tender green-chile chicken for tacos and bowls
description: Chicken cooks gently in salsa verde with beans and corn, then shreds for tacos or rice bowls.

steps.title: Morning start
steps.instruction: Add chicken thighs and salsa verde to the slow cooker, keeping raw chicken away from toppings.

steps.title: Cook low
steps.instruction: Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours without opening the lid repeatedly.

steps.title: Warm beans
steps.instruction: Rinse beans and stir them in for the final hour so they do not break apart.

steps.title: Check temperature
steps.instruction: Check the thickest thigh reaches 165°F before removing it to shred.

steps.title: Shred chicken
steps.instruction: Shred chicken with two forks and return it to the salsa so each piece stays juicy.

steps.title: Add corn
steps.instruction: Stir in corn and cook until it is hot throughout, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Taste salsa
steps.instruction: Taste the sauce and add lime juice; add salt only after tasting the salsa verde.

steps.title: Warm tortillas
steps.instruction: Wrap tortillas in foil and warm at 200°F until flexible, not crisp.

steps.title: Hold safely
steps.instruction: Keep chicken on warm above 140°F and keep cheese and sour cream cold.

steps.title: Serve bar
steps.instruction: Offer chicken in tortillas or bowls with beans, corn, lime, and toppings.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover the chicken thighs — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. Keep the cheese and sour cream cold the whole time — they don't belong anywhere near that hold cabinet. On return, spot-check the chicken at a safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Chicken thighs and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Use thighs because they stay tender on warm.
Keep mild and hot salsa separate.
Drain excess sauce for less messy tacos.
tonightSpread: Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Chicken thighs in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It has a hands-off morning start and adapts to whatever tortillas or rice are on hand.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: portion toppings one day ahead. Storage: refrigerate chicken 3 days. Reheating: heat chicken to 165°F.
substitutions: Use pinto beans for black beans.
